title: Combine Stakeholder Names with UNION
description_markdown: Combine the distinct set of first names from both `employees` and `customers` into a unified list named `person_first_name` using `UNION`. Order alphabetically by `person_first_name` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Combine queries using UNION
SELECT first_name AS person_first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1
UNION
SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 2
ORDER BY ...
solution_query: SELECT first_name AS person_first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 UNION SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 2 ORDER BY person_first_name ASC;
solution_explanation: UNION stacks matching column types from both SELECT queries and deduplicates identical records.
hints: Use UNION between the two SELECT statements.
Order at the very end: `ORDER BY person_first_name ASC`.
Query: SELECT first_name AS person_first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 UNION SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 2 ORDER BY person_first_name ASC;

title: Preserve All Records with UNION ALL
description_markdown: Select `role` as `role_title` from `assignments` for project 101, combined with all `job_title` as `role_title` from `employees` using `UNION ALL`. Do not deduplicate. Order by `role_title` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Use UNION ALL
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT role AS role_title FROM assignments WHERE project_id = 101 UNION ALL SELECT job_title AS role_title FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 ORDER BY role_title ASC;
solution_explanation: UNION ALL combines both record streams without the performance cost of deduplication, retaining all duplicates.
hints: Use UNION ALL between the queries.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.
Query: SELECT role AS role_title FROM assignments WHERE project_id = 101 UNION ALL SELECT job_title AS role_title FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 ORDER BY role_title ASC;

title: Create Tagged Financial Stream Ledger
description_markdown: From `departments`, create a tagged stream: select `dept_name` as `entity_name`, `budget` as `amount`, and `'BUDGET'` as `stream_type`. Union this with `projects`: `project_name` as `entity_name`, `budget` as `amount`, and `'PROJECT_CAPITAL'` as `stream_type`. Order by `amount` DESC, `entity_name` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Union tagged records
SELECT ...
solution_query: SELECT dept_name AS entity_name, budget AS amount, 'BUDGET' AS stream_type FROM departments UNION ALL SELECT project_name AS entity_name, budget AS amount, 'PROJECT_CAPITAL' AS stream_type FROM projects ORDER BY amount DESC, entity_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Injects constant discriminant literals (`'BUDGET'`, `'PROJECT_CAPITAL'`) to distinguish heterogeneous tables in a combined dataset.
hints: Include a literal string column `'BUDGET' AS stream_type` in the first query.
Focus on the required WHERE, JOIN, or GROUP BY clause conditions.

Query: SELECT dept_name AS entity_name, budget AS amount, 'BUDGET' AS stream_type FROM departments UNION ALL SELECT project_name AS entity_name, budget AS amount, 'PROJECT_CAPITAL' AS stream_type FROM projects ORDER BY amount DESC, entity_name ASC;

title: Combine High and Standard Earners with UNION ALL
description_markdown: Use `UNION ALL` to create a categorized roster of employees: combine high earners (`salary >= 170000`) tagged with literal `'High Earner' AS tier` and standard earners (`salary < 100000`) tagged with `'Standard Earner' AS tier`. Return `emp_id`, `first_name`, `salary`, and `tier`. Order by `salary` DESC, `emp_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Combine categorized cohorts with UNION ALL
SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 'High Earner' AS tier
FROM employees
WHERE salary >= 170000.00
UNION ALL
SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 'Standard Earner' AS tier
FROM employees
WHERE salary < 100000.00
ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 'High Earner' AS tier FROM employees WHERE salary >= 170000.00 UNION ALL SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 'Standard Earner' AS tier FROM employees WHERE salary < 100000.00 ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: UNION ALL combines two mutually disjoint subsets of employees without incurring the deduplication overhead of UNION.
common_mistakes: Using UNION instead of UNION ALL when explicit duplicate preservation is requested or subsets are disjoint.
interview_tip: When input sets are guaranteed disjoint, UNION ALL is significantly more performant than UNION because it skips the deduplication sort.
hints: Select high earners in the first query with `'High Earner' AS tier`.
Use `UNION ALL` before selecting standard earners with `'Standard Earner' AS tier`.

Query: SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 'High Earner' AS tier FROM employees WHERE salary >= 170000.00 UNION ALL SELECT emp_id, first_name, salary, 'Standard Earner' AS tier FROM employees WHERE salary < 100000.00 ORDER BY salary DESC, emp_id ASC;

title: Deduplicate Names Across Departments with UNION
description_markdown: Using the `UNION` operator to eliminate duplicates, combine the set of `first_name` values of employees in Engineering (`dept_id = 1`) and Sales (`dept_id = 3`). Order by `first_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Deduplicate names across departments using UNION
SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1
UNION
SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 3
ORDER BY first_name ASC;
solution_query: SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 UNION SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 3 ORDER BY first_name ASC;
solution_explanation: UNION automatically filters out any duplicate first names appearing in both departments.
common_mistakes: Placing an ORDER BY on the first query instead of at the very end.
interview_tip: In SQL, an ORDER BY clause applies to the combined result of a set operation and must appear after the final SELECT.
hints: Query 1: `SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1`.
Combine with `UNION` and order by `first_name ASC`.
Query: SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 1 UNION SELECT first_name FROM employees WHERE dept_id = 3 ORDER BY first_name ASC;

title: Merge Customer Registration and Order Activity Dates
description_markdown: Using `UNION ALL`, construct an event log combining customer registrations (`CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS event_date`, tagged with literal `'account_created' AS event_type`) and order dates (`order_date AS event_date`, tagged with `'order_placed' AS event_type`). Return `customer_id`, `event_date`, and `event_type`. Order by `event_date` ASC, `customer_id` ASC, `event_type` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Build unified event log with UNION ALL
SELECT customer_id, CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS event_date, 'account_created' AS event_type
FROM customers
UNION ALL
SELECT customer_id, order_date AS event_date, 'order_placed' AS event_type
FROM orders
ORDER BY event_date ASC, customer_id ASC, event_type ASC;
solution_query: SELECT customer_id, CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS event_date, 'account_created' AS event_type FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT customer_id, order_date AS event_date, 'order_placed' AS event_type FROM orders ORDER BY event_date ASC, customer_id ASC, event_type ASC;
solution_explanation: Casts timestamp to DATE to align data types across both branches of the UNION ALL before sorting chronologically.
common_mistakes: Mismatched data types between created_at (timestamp) and order_date (date).
interview_tip: Set operators require matching or compatible data types in corresponding positional columns.
hints: Use `CAST(created_at AS DATE)` to match the DATE type of `order_date`.
Inject literals `'account_created'` and `'order_placed'`.

Query: SELECT customer_id, CAST(created_at AS DATE) AS event_date, 'account_created' AS event_type FROM customers UNION ALL SELECT customer_id, order_date AS event_date, 'order_placed' AS event_type FROM orders ORDER BY event_date ASC, customer_id ASC, event_type ASC;

title: Find Unique Category References with UNION
description_markdown: Using `UNION`, find all unique category identifier values that appear either as a primary `category_id` or as a non-null `parent_category_id` in the `categories` table. Name the column `cat_id`. Order by `cat_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Unique category IDs across parent and child roles
SELECT category_id AS cat_id FROM categories
UNION
SELECT parent_category_id AS cat_id FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY cat_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT category_id AS cat_id FROM categories UNION SELECT parent_category_id AS cat_id FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY cat_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Collects both child and parent foreign key keys into a single deduplicated domain of category IDs.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to filter out NULL parent_category_id values.
interview_tip: UNION naturally removes NULLs or duplicates present across relational hierarchies.
hints: Select `category_id AS cat_id` from categories.
Union with `parent_category_id AS cat_id` where `parent_category_id IS NOT NULL`.
Query: SELECT category_id AS cat_id FROM categories UNION SELECT parent_category_id AS cat_id FROM categories WHERE parent_category_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY cat_id ASC;

title: Build Campus Directory with UNION ALL
description_markdown: Combine all students (tagged with `'Student' AS campus_role`) and professors (tagged with `'Professor' AS campus_role`) into a single campus directory using `UNION ALL`. Return `first_name`, `last_name`, and `campus_role`. Order by `last_name` ASC, `first_name` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Campus directory via UNION ALL
SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Student' AS campus_role FROM students
UNION ALL
SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Professor' AS campus_role FROM professors
ORDER BY last_name ASC, first_name ASC;
solution_query: SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Student' AS campus_role FROM students UNION ALL SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Professor' AS campus_role FROM professors ORDER BY last_name ASC, first_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Stacks rows from two separate entities with an added literal distinguishing each entity's role.
common_mistakes: Ordering within the first query block.
interview_tip: UNION ALL is standard for creating polymorphic views over normalized separate entity tables.
hints: Select names from students with literal `'Student' AS campus_role`.
Union all with professors with literal `'Professor' AS campus_role`.
Query: SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Student' AS campus_role FROM students UNION ALL SELECT first_name, last_name, 'Professor' AS campus_role FROM professors ORDER BY last_name ASC, first_name ASC;

title: Collect Distinct Academic Departments Using UNION
description_markdown: Use `UNION` to return a distinct list of all academic department names that appear in either the `professors` table or the `courses` table. Order alphabetically by `department` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Unique departments across professors and courses
SELECT department FROM professors
UNION
SELECT department FROM courses
ORDER BY department ASC;
solution_query: SELECT department FROM professors UNION SELECT department FROM courses ORDER BY department ASC;
solution_explanation: Performs set union of department strings across faculty and course schedules, eliminating duplicate strings.
common_mistakes: Using UNION ALL which would repeat department names.
interview_tip: UNION performs a distinct sort across both branches, ideal for compiling global lookup lists.
hints: Select `department` from `professors`.
Use `UNION` before `SELECT department FROM courses`.
Query: SELECT department FROM professors UNION SELECT department FROM courses ORDER BY department ASC;

title: Segregate Completed and Refunded Orders with Status Flags
description_markdown: Using `UNION ALL`, combine completed orders (`order_status = 'completed'`, flagged with `'COMPLETED' AS status_flag`) and refunded orders (`order_status = 'refunded'`, flagged with `'REFUNDED' AS status_flag`). Return `order_id`, `customer_id`, `total_amount`, and `status_flag`. Order by `order_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Combine completed and refunded orders via UNION ALL
SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount, 'COMPLETED' AS status_flag
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'completed'
UNION ALL
SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount, 'REFUNDED' AS status_flag
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'refunded'
ORDER BY order_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount, 'COMPLETED' AS status_flag FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'completed' UNION ALL SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount, 'REFUNDED' AS status_flag FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'refunded' ORDER BY order_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Partitions orders by status criteria and concatenates the two streams with clear audit classification tags.
common_mistakes: Filtering both conditions into a single WHERE clause without the status_flag distinction.
interview_tip: UNION ALL allows different SELECT clauses to apply specific business tags before merging.
hints: First branch filters `order_status = 'completed'` with `'COMPLETED' AS status_flag`.
Second branch filters `order_status = 'refunded'` with `'REFUNDED' AS status_flag`.

Query: SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount, 'COMPLETED' AS status_flag FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'completed' UNION ALL SELECT order_id, customer_id, total_amount, 'REFUNDED' AS status_flag FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'refunded' ORDER BY order_id ASC;

title: Unique Professional Titles Across Staff and Assignments
description_markdown: Using `UNION`, compile a comprehensive distinct list of all professional job titles and assignment roles by combining `job_title AS title_name` from `employees` and `role AS title_name` from `assignments`. Order alphabetically by `title_name` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Unique professional roles via UNION
SELECT job_title AS title_name FROM employees
UNION
SELECT role AS title_name FROM assignments
ORDER BY title_name ASC;
solution_query: SELECT job_title AS title_name FROM employees UNION SELECT role AS title_name FROM assignments ORDER BY title_name ASC;
solution_explanation: Consolidates company positions and project-specific roles into a unified deduplicated terminology list.
common_mistakes: Mismatched alias names between branches (column name of first branch sets the result column name).
interview_tip: In SQL set operations, the column names of the first SELECT statement dictate the column names of the final result set.
hints: Select `job_title AS title_name` from employees.
Union with `role AS title_name` from assignments.
Query: SELECT job_title AS title_name FROM employees UNION SELECT role AS title_name FROM assignments ORDER BY title_name ASC;

title: Reconcile Invoices and Payments with UNION ALL
description_markdown: Generate an audit reconciliation stream using `UNION ALL`. Combine orders (`total_amount AS amount`, tagged with `'ORDER_INVOICE' AS txn_type`) with successful payments from `payments` (`amount`, where `payment_status = 'success'`, tagged with `'PAYMENT_RECEIVED' AS txn_type`). Return `order_id`, `amount`, and `txn_type`. Order by `order_id` ASC, `txn_type` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Financial reconciliation stream via UNION ALL
SELECT order_id, total_amount AS amount, 'ORDER_INVOICE' AS txn_type
FROM orders
UNION ALL
SELECT order_id, amount, 'PAYMENT_RECEIVED' AS txn_type
FROM payments
WHERE payment_status = 'success'
ORDER BY order_id ASC, txn_type ASC;
solution_query: SELECT order_id, total_amount AS amount, 'ORDER_INVOICE' AS txn_type FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT order_id, amount, 'PAYMENT_RECEIVED' AS txn_type FROM payments WHERE payment_status = 'success' ORDER BY order_id ASC, txn_type ASC;
solution_explanation: Unifies debit and credit records across orders and payment gateways into a double-entry style audit stream.
common_mistakes: Leaving off the payment_status = 'success' filter on payments.
interview_tip: Double-entry general ledgers in fintech are built using UNION ALL to stitch debits and credits together.
hints: Select orders with `'ORDER_INVOICE' AS txn_type`.
Union all with successful payments tagged as `'PAYMENT_RECEIVED' AS txn_type`.

Query: SELECT order_id, total_amount AS amount, 'ORDER_INVOICE' AS txn_type FROM orders UNION ALL SELECT order_id, amount, 'PAYMENT_RECEIVED' AS txn_type FROM payments WHERE payment_status = 'success' ORDER BY order_id ASC, txn_type ASC;

title: Consolidate Academic Fields of Study via UNION
description_markdown: Using `UNION`, produce a distinct list of all declared academic study areas: combine `major AS academic_area` from `students` (excluding `'Undeclared'`) with `department AS academic_area` from `courses`. Order alphabetically by `academic_area` ascending.

SELECT major AS academic_area FROM students WHERE major != 'Undeclared'
UNION
SELECT department AS academic_area FROM courses
ORDER BY academic_area ASC;
solution_query: SELECT major AS academic_area FROM students WHERE major != 'Undeclared' UNION SELECT department AS academic_area FROM courses ORDER BY academic_area ASC;
solution_explanation: Collects student degree majors and course departmental offerings into a single deduplicated discipline taxonomy.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to filter out 'Undeclared' from the student roster.
interview_tip: Set operations are often used to consolidate disparate domain registries across multiple operational databases.
hints: Filter `major != 'Undeclared'` in the first query.
UNION with `SELECT department AS academic_area FROM courses`.
Query: SELECT major AS academic_area FROM students WHERE major != 'Undeclared' UNION SELECT department AS academic_area FROM courses ORDER BY academic_area ASC;

title: HR Career Milestone Timeline with UNION ALL
description_markdown: Construct an HR career event timeline using `UNION ALL`. Combine initial hiring events from `employees` (`emp_id`, `hire_date AS event_date`, literal `'NEW_HIRE' AS event_name`) with compensation milestones from `salaries_history` (`emp_id`, `effective_date AS event_date`, `change_reason AS event_name`). Order by `event_date` ASC, `emp_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- HR milestone timeline via UNION ALL
SELECT emp_id, hire_date AS event_date, 'NEW_HIRE' AS event_name
FROM employees
UNION ALL
SELECT emp_id, effective_date AS event_date, change_reason AS event_name
FROM salaries_history
ORDER BY event_date ASC, emp_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT emp_id, hire_date AS event_date, 'NEW_HIRE' AS event_name FROM employees UNION ALL SELECT emp_id, effective_date AS event_date, change_reason AS event_name FROM salaries_history ORDER BY event_date ASC, emp_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Blends two time-series tables into a unified chronological log of employment events.
common_mistakes: Mismatched date types or forgetting to sort by event_date.
interview_tip: Chronological activity streams are created by taking projections of distinct event tables and combining with UNION ALL.
hints: Select hire_date from employees with `'NEW_HIRE'`.
Union all with effective_date and change_reason from salaries_history.

Query: SELECT emp_id, hire_date AS event_date, CAST('NEW_HIRE' AS VARCHAR(100)) AS event_name FROM employees UNION ALL SELECT emp_id, effective_date AS event_date, change_reason AS event_name FROM salaries_history ORDER BY event_date ASC, emp_id ASC;

title: Find Unique Customers Across Distinct Product Categories
description_markdown: Using `UNION`, find all distinct `customer_id` values for customers who ordered Computers (`category_id = 2`) OR ordered Coffee & Tea (`category_id = 6`). Join `orders`, `order_items`, and `products` within each query branch. Order by `customer_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Unique customers across two distinct categories via UNION
SELECT o.customer_id
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.category_id = 2
UNION
SELECT o.customer_id
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE p.category_id = 6
ORDER BY customer_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category_id = 2 UNION SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category_id = 6 ORDER BY customer_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Performs set union of customer IDs meeting category condition 2 or category condition 6, eliminating duplicate customer IDs.
common_mistakes: Using OR across a complex join when query plans prefer indexed UNION branch evaluation.
interview_tip: In database query optimization, transforming complex OR predicates into indexed UNION queries often unlocks massive speedups.
hints: Branch 1 joins orders, order_items, and products where `category_id = 2`.
Branch 2 does the same where `category_id = 6`.

Query: SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category_id = 2 UNION SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.category_id = 6 ORDER BY customer_id ASC;

title: Unpivot Price and Cost Columns into Single Stream
description_markdown: Unpivot the `price` and `cost` columns from `products` into a single stream using `UNION ALL`. First select `product_id`, `product_name`, `price AS amount`, and literal `'RETAIL' AS valuation_type`. Union with `product_id`, `product_name`, `cost AS amount`, and `'COST' AS valuation_type`. Order by `product_id` ASC, `valuation_type` DESC.
starter_query:
-- Unpivot price and cost columns using UNION ALL
SELECT product_id, product_name, price AS amount, 'RETAIL' AS valuation_type
FROM products
UNION ALL
SELECT product_id, product_name, cost AS amount, 'COST' AS valuation_type
FROM products
ORDER BY product_id ASC, valuation_type DESC;
solution_query: SELECT product_id, product_name, price AS amount, 'RETAIL' AS valuation_type FROM products UNION ALL SELECT product_id, product_name, cost AS amount, 'COST' AS valuation_type FROM products ORDER BY product_id ASC, valuation_type DESC;
solution_explanation: Converts a wide table format (having both price and cost columns) into a normalized long table format via UNION ALL.
common_mistakes: Using UNION which might deduplicate items where cost equals price.
interview_tip: UNION ALL is the standard cross-dialect technique for UNPIVOT operations in ANSI SQL.
hints: First query selects `price AS amount` with `'RETAIL'`.
Second query selects `cost AS amount` with `'COST'`.

Query: SELECT product_id, product_name, price AS amount, 'RETAIL' AS valuation_type FROM products UNION ALL SELECT product_id, product_name, cost AS amount, 'COST' AS valuation_type FROM products ORDER BY product_id ASC, valuation_type DESC;

title: Compile Honors and Senior Cohort with UNION
description_markdown: Using `UNION`, create a deduplicated list of students who either achieved academic honors (`gpa >= 3.80`) OR entered the college in `enrollment_year = 2021`. Return `student_id`, `first_name`, and `gpa`. Order by `student_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Distinct students across GPA and enrollment year criteria
SELECT student_id, first_name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa >= 3.80
UNION
SELECT student_id, first_name, gpa FROM students WHERE enrollment_year = 2021
ORDER BY student_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT student_id, first_name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa >= 3.80 UNION SELECT student_id, first_name, gpa FROM students WHERE enrollment_year = 2021 ORDER BY student_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Ensures students who satisfy both conditions (honor roll AND entered in 2021) appear exactly once in the final result set.
common_mistakes: Using UNION ALL, which would list qualifying dual-criteria students twice.
interview_tip: UNION is mathematically equivalent to the set union operator (A ∪ B), deduplicating elements in the intersection.
hints: Select students where `gpa >= 3.80`.
Union with students where `enrollment_year = 2021`.
Query: SELECT student_id, first_name, gpa FROM students WHERE gpa >= 3.80 UNION SELECT student_id, first_name, gpa FROM students WHERE enrollment_year = 2021 ORDER BY student_id ASC;

title: Combine Department and Project Capital Commitments
description_markdown: Using `UNION ALL`, combine departmental budgets from `departments` (`dept_id`, `budget`, tagged with `'DEPARTMENT' AS entity_type`) and project budgets from `projects` (`dept_id`, `budget`, tagged with `'PROJECT' AS entity_type`). Filter out any rows with NULL `dept_id` or NULL `budget`. Order by `dept_id` ASC, `budget` DESC.
starter_query:
-- Financial capital commitments via UNION ALL
SELECT dept_id, budget, 'DEPARTMENT' AS entity_type
FROM departments
WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL AND budget IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT dept_id, budget, 'PROJECT' AS entity_type
FROM projects
WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL AND budget IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY dept_id ASC, budget DESC;
solution_query: SELECT dept_id, budget, 'DEPARTMENT' AS entity_type FROM departments WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL AND budget IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT dept_id, budget, 'PROJECT' AS entity_type FROM projects WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL AND budget IS NOT NULL ORDER BY dept_id ASC, budget DESC;
solution_explanation: Builds a unified ledger of capital allocations across operational departments and specific initiative projects.
common_mistakes: Leaving off the NULL check on budget.
interview_tip: Combining financial commitments from differing tiers is a frequent reporting pattern.
hints: Branch 1 selects from departments with `'DEPARTMENT' AS entity_type`.
Branch 2 selects from projects with `'PROJECT' AS entity_type`.

Query: SELECT dept_id, budget, 'DEPARTMENT' AS entity_type FROM departments WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL AND budget IS NOT NULL UNION ALL SELECT dept_id, budget, 'PROJECT' AS entity_type FROM projects WHERE dept_id IS NOT NULL AND budget IS NOT NULL ORDER BY dept_id ASC, budget DESC;

title: Gather Distinct Catalog and Engaged Product IDs
description_markdown: Using `UNION`, find all unique `product_id` numbers that are currently marked active (`is_active = TRUE` in `products`) OR have received at least one review in the `reviews` table. Order by `product_id` ascending.

solution_query: SELECT product_id FROM products WHERE is_active = TRUE UNION SELECT product_id FROM reviews ORDER BY product_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Collects active inventory items and engaged products that have reviews, deduplicating IDs across both sets.

interview_tip: Set operations compile universe sets across distinct operational conditions without joining overhead.
hints: Select `product_id` from products where `is_active = TRUE`.
Union with `SELECT product_id FROM reviews`.

title: Faculty Compensation Roll-Up by Rank with UNION ALL
description_markdown: Using `UNION ALL`, partition and label faculty members by their professional rank: select full faculty (`title LIKE '%Professor%'`, tagged with `'Full Faculty' AS status`) and adjunct staff (`title LIKE '%Lecturer%'`, tagged with `'Adjunct' AS status`). Return `professor_id`, `first_name`, `salary`, and `status`. Order by `salary` DESC, `professor_id` ASC.
starter_query:
-- Faculty rank compensation ledger via UNION ALL
SELECT professor_id, first_name, salary, 'Full Faculty' AS status
FROM professors
WHERE title LIKE '%Professor%'
UNION ALL
SELECT professor_id, first_name, salary, 'Adjunct' AS status
FROM professors
WHERE title LIKE '%Lecturer%'
ORDER BY salary DESC, professor_id ASC;
solution_query: SELECT professor_id, first_name, salary, 'Full Faculty' AS status FROM professors WHERE title LIKE '%Professor%' UNION ALL SELECT professor_id, first_name, salary, 'Adjunct' AS status FROM professors WHERE title LIKE '%Lecturer%' ORDER BY salary DESC, professor_id ASC;
solution_explanation: Splits faculty by rank and combines them into an ordered compensation breakdown.
common_mistakes: Using AND in a single WHERE clause instead of splitting into distinct union branches.
interview_tip: UNION ALL makes complex multi-tier reporting transparent and easily maintainable.
hints: Branch 1 matches `title LIKE '%Professor%'` with status `'Full Faculty'`.
Branch 2 matches `title LIKE '%Lecturer%'` with status `'Adjunct'`.

Query: SELECT professor_id, first_name, salary, 'Full Faculty' AS status FROM professors WHERE title LIKE '%Professor%' UNION ALL SELECT professor_id, first_name, salary, 'Adjunct' AS status FROM professors WHERE title LIKE '%Lecturer%' ORDER BY salary DESC, professor_id ASC;

title: Compile Target Audience via UNION
description_markdown: Using `UNION`, create a target marketing list of customers who are located in the United States (`country = 'USA'`) OR who have completed at least one order (`order_status = 'completed'`). Return `customer_id` and `email`. Order by `customer_id` ascending.
starter_query:
-- Target audience compile via UNION
